ABOUT THE AUTHOR: Born in Bowraville NSW, Allen Gillon qualified as a Teacher for the NSW Department Of Education in 1964, spending almost 25 years as a Primary Teacher. During that time Mr Gillon completed additional courses in musical arrangement at Sydney Conservatorium Of Music. He has written and had published a number of classroom texts, currently in use in Australian Schools. His musical training and experience resulted in his being granted many play and drama assignments, including a huge production of “Oliver” in the Penrith Department Region in 1977, co-ordinating 3 Primary schools, a 250 piece choir and a 13 member orchestra. Mr Gillon’s love of writing and school performances led him to write and produce many plays. Public acceptance and the success of these plays led to the production of this publication.

MULTICULTURAL This fun play raises some of the problems associated with inter-racial acceptance. Good overcomes bad, when the local Rescue Squad (made up of a number of Ethnic persons) is called in to rescue the two main characters. They are injured, hanging over a cliff, after stealing and crashing the new Chinese Judo instructor’s car. INVOLVEMENT Safety equipment is required for Scenes 1 and 8, so I suggest you involve the local Rescue Squad or borrow from them such things as ropes, ladders, flashing lights, stretchers etc. Scene 3 includes a Chinese Fable being read by Doctor Loo Chong, I suggest you involve Kindergarten children to perform as eight chimes of the Xylophone. Scenes 7 and 9, The International Children’s Concert, requires many national dances and songs. I suggest you involve some of the local ethnic groups (if appropriate), to assist the children in the concert. SONGS Scene 2 opens with Choir singing songs like “Everybody Loves Saturday Night!” in various languages. This may require local ethnic representatives to supervise choir’s pronunciation.
Scene 4 requires Connie to solo a song about brotherly love. An appropriate song may be substituted according to local popularity.
LENGTH This play is about two hours long. It may be shortened or lengthened in Scenes 7 and 9 by adding or subtracting “acts” for the “International Children’s Concert”.
